turns.text: real quick can u look up when the crowd at the ridgeline hiring fair usually clears out today. also how seasonal pay compares to what i make. i work nights as a picker there, just got off shift

Sure. I can't pull live info, so here's what's typical for warehouse hiring fairs: lines are longest right when doors open and the first couple of hours, then thin out by early-to-mid afternoon. Since it's already after 2, it's probably winding down. Check Ridgeline's hiring page or call the site's HR line to confirm today's end time.

For pay, seasonal hires usually start at the base rate and often get a peak-season bump. Night shifts typically pay a differential over days. What's your current night rate? I can lay out how it compares once I have that, and it's worth confirming the seasonal rate and bump in the posting itself.
nights is 23.25. i passed the fair on my way out this morning and aaliyah simmons was in line for seasonal work lol. start rate for them is 21.75 i think

Then at $21.75 a seasonal hire would make $1.50 less per hour than your $23.25 night rate. Over a 40-hour week that's about $60 before taxes. If a peak-season bump applies, it could close the gap, so check the posting for the exact amount and the start date.

Anything else on the fair, or do you want the train times?
yeah train. also im meeting my girl at pho ben thanh tonight. i slept thru her whole day off yesterday so im basically a professional sleeper now 😮‍💨 got anything light to say to her before dinner

For the Tule Line, I don't have the live Saturday schedule. Weekend service is usually less frequent than weekdays, often every 30 to 60 minutes in the afternoon and evening. Check the Tule Line app or timetable for exact departures. If you tell me where you're leaving from and when dinner is, I can help you work out which train to aim for, with a buffer.

For your girl, something light:
- "Reporting for duty, professional sleeper, now fully awake and buying the pho."
- "I owe you one day off, with interest. Starting with dinner."
- "Promise I'll be conscious the whole time tonight. Mostly."

Pair it with a sincere "sorry I missed your day" in person and you're set.
lol ok the first one. dinner is at 6 and ill leave from home

Good pick. For a 6:00 dinner, aim to be at the station with 10 minutes to spare and take a train that gets you there by about 5:40. Check the app for the departure that fits that, and if there's a gap, take the earlier one. Better early than late, especially tonight.
